verdict: Native plain OpenAI streaming tool-only replies use a direct second HTTP body, not WireBodySpool. Broader acceptance remains open.
scope: Native indexed plain toolFormat=openai only. Kimi/Mistral and other providers retain their explicit legacy routes.

reproduction.result: 0 pass, 3 fail, 6 assertions; all three fail operation-created continuation directory receipt.

productionClosure.http: 69 tests, 759 assertions. 23 histories x none/all/allButLast; actual two HTTP posts with exact legacy-route SHA256, byte count and Content-Length, zero operation files, one emitted tool call and terminal text.
productionClosure.ownership: 10 lifecycle cases cover both prepared initial stream flags, pending user, trailing tool-media flush, duplicate/empty current IDs, repeated reader retry, unsent idempotence, release rejection, abort-before-build identity, awaited paused-reader retirement and transport-error retry.
productionClosure.limitation: Actual two-post tests use the real OpenAI provider; public ChatSession tests refreshed separately still exercise a one-post text response. Continuation terminal history commitment is not independently tested here.

mechanism.planning: Capture source and continuation facts during initial preparation. Build measures only buildContinuationTail SDK messages and composes their six-state transfer summary with the captured prefix, then finalizes media/comma state. Emission rereads the same selected source once per send. No prefix counting pass during build, copied history source, whole-history array, whole-body string or prefix-wide tool-ID set.
mechanism.reasoningDecision: Expanded corpus exposed thinking-only-chain: legacy omitReasoning disables reasoning inclusion but preserves empty assistant messages under none/allButLast. Always stripping blocks lost 34 bytes. Exact old bytes require captured original strip policy plus includeInContext=false. When inclusion was true and strip is not all, initial preparation acquires that distinct registered format once. Other cases reuse the original plan. Warm/build reuse these facts; no new registration occurs at continuation build. This necessary cold-format fill is an explicit departure from the requested unconditional strip-all assumption.
mechanism.cleanup: Continuation body uses shared ChatHttpBody surface without file paths. Release is awaitable in stream finally and request cleanup. Request retirement closes initial plus all outstanding continuation readers before external pin ownership can retire. Released requests refuse new builds.
mechanism.planningCost: Warm 40/4000 preparation test uses the actual journal descriptor read counter and observes zero reads during continuation build plus unsent repeated release. Initial source capture/cold fills and emission are outside that build interval. Selected changed-view planning and metadata cost beyond this domain are not newly measured.

controls.matchedPredicate: Two-received-requests matcher: only one request arrived. This does not independently establish wrong-reasoning byte sensitivity after a complete second POST.

controls.name: wrong-tail-comma
controls.matchedPredicate: Independent complete-body SHA256 matcher at unchanged length: expected ed7a91fff4632bed7925eae9083ddf889c8d6311ebdbd585bfa496e9afd0b7b2; received 53085841c777b545a42f6d68cd001a6bbc5a6819cde22604b9984bd5581f6122.

controls.name: dropped-tail
controls.matchedPredicate: Independent Content-Length matcher: expected 567 bytes, received 460 bytes. This control removes the final continuation tail message, not specifically the tool-call acknowledgement.

controls.name: source-close-first-response
controls.matchedPredicate: Two-received-requests matcher: only one request arrived after closing the source during initial emission.

interruptedControls: Two zero-length-comma controls stopped at 120s inactivity / 100s command limits and are excluded. Source restored by cmp and matching SHA256. Accepted comma control substitutes semicolon at unchanged byte length, so the actual independent HTTP SHA assertion detects it. Dropped-tail control adjusts declared length to its shortened body; independent expected bytes detect the omission.
